items.title: Three equivalent descriptions of when a single element is elementary over a generated subsystem
items.author: Silvia Barbina; Enrique Casanovas
items.work: The elementary theory of free Steiner triple systems
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 876-883: for an infinite unconfined system, a generated subsystem A and an element outside it, three conditions are equivalent, namely that the closure of the element is itself for some ordering with A as initial segment, that A is elementary in Aa and Aa is elementary in M, and that in some saturated elementary extension there is a binary tree above the element whose closure is the subsystem. The proof (source lines 884-892) is a four-step cycle in which each step is a different mechanism: moving an element to the bottom of an ordering, reading an ordering off an elementary chain, realising a type in a saturated extension, and using the tree lemma to move the ordering so that the closure of the element becomes the element itself. The statement records the three conditions and the extra consequence, and none of the four mechanisms.
